worked_solution:
The gradient of the product of two functions $f(x,y)$ and $g(x,y)$ is given by:

$$
∇[fg]=f\,∇\,g+g\,∇\,f
$$

First, we calculate the first order partial derivatives of $f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{x+y})={e}^{x+y} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{x+y})={e}^{x+y}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\text{ }i+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\text{ }j={e}^{x+y}\text{ }i+{e}^{x+y}\text{ }j.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the partial derivatives of $g(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})=2x \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})=2y\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇g(x,y) & =\frac{∂g}{∂x}\text{ }i+\frac{∂g}{∂y}\text{ }j=2x\text{ }i+2y\text{ }j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the product rule, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇[f(x,y)g(x,y)] & =({e}^{x+y})(2x\text{ }i+2y\text{ }j)+({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})({e}^{x+y}\text{ }i+{e}^{x+y}\text{ }j) \\  & =2x{e}^{x+y}\text{ }i+2y{e}^{x+y}\text{ }j+({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}){e}^{x+y}\text{ }i+({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}){e}^{x+y}\text{ }j \\  & =({x}^{2}+2x+{y}^{2}){e}^{x+y}\text{ }i+({x}^{2}+2y+{y}^{2}){e}^{x+y}\text{ }j\end{aligned}
$$
html:
The gradient of the product of two functions f(x,y) and g(x,y) is given by:

∇[fg]=f∇g+g∇f

First, we calculate the first order partial derivatives of f(x,y):

∂f∂x=∂∂x(ex+y)=ex+y∂f∂y=∂∂y(ex+y)=ex+y

Hence, ∇f(x,y)=∂f∂x i+∂f∂y j=ex+y i+ex+y j.

Next, we calculate the partial derivatives of g(x,y):

∂g∂x=∂∂x(x2+y2)=2x∂g∂y=∂∂y(x2+y2)=2y

Therefore, ∇g(x,y)=∂g∂x i+∂g∂y j=2x i+2y j.

Finally, using the product rule, we obtain:

∇[f(x,y)g(x,y)]=(ex+y)(2x i+2y j)+(x2+y2)(ex+y i+ex+y j)=2xex+y i+2yex+y j+(x2+y2)ex+y i+(x2+y2)ex+y j=(x2+2x+y2)ex+y i+(x2+2y+y2)ex+y j
